mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in liquidity and an increase in borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDP growth, or if the correlation between GDP growth and 60-day returns is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is positive over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in one month indicates a contraction in the supply side of the economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO falls > 1%, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 20-day returns is positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economic environment, which boosts investor confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 rises and UNRATE falls, or if the joint effect of GDPC1 and UNRATE changes on 20-day returns is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in one month signals inflationary pressures, which can lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5%, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL changes and 20-day returns is positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in one month signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances when PAYEMS falls > 100k, or if the correlation between PAYEMS changes and 5-day returns is positive over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 and HOUST both rise, or if the joint effect of GDPC1 and HOUST changes on 60-day returns is negative over a 3-year rolling window.
